q.t: Any substance used to make an object is called a…
q.e: Paper, wood, glass, metal and plastic are materials.

q.t: Arranging objects into groups is called…
q.e: Grouping is based on a common property.

q.t: Shiny materials are called…
q.e: Metals are usually lustrous.

q.t: Glass and water are…
q.e: You can see clearly through them.

q.t: Butter paper and frosted glass are…
q.e: You see objects, but not clearly.

q.t: Wood and metal sheets are…
q.e: You can't see through them.

q.t: Sugar in water is…
q.e: It dissolves and disappears.

q.t: Sand in water is…
q.e: It stays visible however long you stir.

q.t: Anything that occupies space and has mass is…
q.e: Even air is matter.

q.t: The space occupied by a material is its…
q.e: Measured in litres, millilitres or cubic metres.

q.t: Which two properties do ALL materials have?
q.e: Not everything is shiny or soluble, but everything has mass and takes up space.

q.t: Is air matter?
o: Yes — it occupies space and has mass
q.e: Being invisible doesn't stop it being matter.

q.t: Why do metals sometimes look dull?
o: Air and moisture act on their surface
q.e: A freshly cut surface shows the lustre best.

q.t: 'All that glitters is not gold' means…
o: Not everything shiny is a metal
q.e: Some surfaces are made shiny by polishing or coatings.

q.t: Rubber is harder than sponge but softer than iron. This shows hardness is…
q.e: 'Hard' only makes sense as 'harder than what?'

q.t: Oil and water left undisturbed…
q.e: Some liquids don't mix with water.

q.t: Why is oxygen dissolving in water important?
o: Water animals and plants need it to survive
q.e: Fish breathe dissolved oxygen.

q.t: Why is a tumbler not made of cloth?
q.e: We choose materials based on properties and purpose.

q.t: The SI unit of volume is…
Which is written correctly?
q.e: Lowercase, no 's', no full stop, with a space.

q.t: How many litres are in 1 m³?
A 500 mL bottle holds how many litres?
How do you make ORS without a packet?
o: 6 tsp sugar + ½ tsp salt in 1 L boiled, cooled water
q.e: ORS treats dehydration from diarrhoea.

q.t: Why are different balls made for different sports?
o: Each sport needs a different bounce
q.e: Material is chosen for the property needed.

q.t: A pen made of plastic, metal and ink shows…
o: One object can have several materials
q.e: Objects are often made of several materials.

q.t: Why is classification useful?
o: It helps us study patterns in properties
q.e: Grouping helps us observe patterns.

q.t: Baked clay is called…
q.e: Clay baked in kilns becomes terracotta.

q.t: How old is the earliest pottery in the Indian subcontinent?
q.e: Found at Lahuradewa and Mehrgarh.

q.t: Mass tells us…
q.e: More mass = heavier. Units: g and kg.

q.t: Chalk powder in water is…
q.e: It stays visible and doesn't dissolve.

q.t: Which is NOT a property every material has?
q.e: Many materials are not shiny, but all have mass and volume.

q.t: A scratch test with a key leaves a mark on wood but not on steel. So…
q.e: Hard materials are difficult to scratch.

q.t: Why is water so important in the body's working?
o: It dissolves a large number of materials
q.e: Water carries dissolved substances around the body.

q.t: Two identical tumblers with water to different levels hold different…
q.e: Volume is the space occupied.

q.t: Which is written correctly for millilitre?
q.e: Lowercase m, capital L, a space, no s, no full stop.

q.t: A silver-coloured shiny spoon could be plastic. Why?
o: Surfaces can be coated to shine
q.e: Not everything shiny is a metal.

q.t: A grocer keeps spices together and pulses together. This is…
q.e: Grouping by a common property.

q.t: Ayurveda describes matter using how many properties (guṇa)?
q.e: 20 properties in ten pairs of opposites.

q.t: Two students group objects differently — one by colour, one by material. Which is correct?
q.e: The useful question is which property matters for your purpose.

q.t: 1.5 L = how many mL?
